t:
(a) In General.—The Secretary shall carry out a program of research, development, demonstration, and commercial application to—
        (1) address energy-related issues associated with provision of adequate water supplies, optimal management, and efficient use of water;  
        (2) address water-related issues associated with the provision of adequate supplies, optimal management, and efficient use of energy; and  
        (3) assess the effectiveness of existing programs within the Department and other Federal agencies to address these energy and water related issues.   
    (b) Program Elements.—The program under this section shall include—
        (1) arsenic treatment;  
        (2) desalination; and  
        (3) planning, analysis, and modeling of energy and water supply and demand.   
    (c) Collaboration.—In carrying out this section, the Secretary shall consult with the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency, the Secretary of the Interior, the Chief Engineer of the Army Corps of Engineers, the Secretary of Commerce, the Secretary of Defense, and other Federal agencies as appropriate.  
    (d) Facilities.—The Secretary may utilize all existing facilities within the Department and may design and construct additional facilities as needed to carry out the purposes of this program.  
    (e) Advisory Committee.—The Secretary shall establish or utilize an advisory committee to provide independent advice and review of the program. 
    (f) Reports.—Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report on the assessment described in subsection (b) and recommendations for future actions.

fable.w: Subsection (e) requires the Secretary to establish or use an advisory committee giving "independent advice and review" of the program, which implies members from outside the Department advising on a federal program. The tempting reading is "No", because subsection (c) is consultation only among federal agencies and subsection (f) is a report to Congress, and neither crosses the federal boundary. The advisory committee does bring outsiders in, although its membership is not spelled out, so some uncertainty remains.
fable.s: (e) Advisory Committee.—The Secretary shall establish or utilize an advisory committee to provide independent advice and review of the program.

opus.w: Subsection (e) requires the Secretary to set up or use an advisory committee to give independent advice and review of the program. That brings outside advisers into federal decisions about the program, which matches the definition's advisory-committee category. The tempting signal, the 'Collaboration' heading in subsection (c), fails because everyone consulted there is a federal agency, and the report to Congress in (f) also stays inside the government.
opus.s: (e) Advisory Committee.—The Secretary shall establish or utilize an advisory committee to provide independent advice and review of the program.
opus.b:
I'm labelling this **Yes**, mainly because of subsection (e), which requires an advisory committee.

**The tempting misreading:** Subsection (c), headed "Collaboration", looks like participation. It isn't. Everyone the Secretary must consult there is a federal agency or official, so that coordination stays inside the government. The report to Congress in (f) is also inside the government.

**What actually counts:** Subsection (e) requires an advisory committee that gives "independent advice and review" of the program. "Independent" points to members from outside the Department, and the worked examples count advisory boards as participation even when the members aren't named. One doubt remains: the statute never says the members must come from outside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary to establish or utilize an advisory committee to provide independent advice. Advisory committees generally consist of non-federal experts or stakeholders, constituting participation by people outside the federal government. While subsection (c) involves intra-agency consultation (which is not participation), subsection (e) clearly mandates a process involving outside parties.
qwen_chat.s: (e) Advisory Committee.—The Secretary shall establish or utilize an advisory committee to provide independent advice and review of the program.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue "No" because subsection (c) describes consultation between federal agencies (Secretary of Energy with EPA, Interior, etc.), which is intra-governmental and thus excluded. However, subsection (e) explicitly requires an advisory committee, which typically involves outside experts, making the answer "Yes". The presence of *any* participation mechanism triggers a "Yes".
